headline: OnePlus exits US and Europe ends phone sales
summary: OnePlus will no longer sell phones in North America or Europe.
details: OnePlus has announced it will no longer launch new products in North America or Europe. The decision was described as a 'strategic decision to focus our efforts' by Oppo, OnePlus's parent company.
The move doesn't affect existing customers, who will still receive after-sales support, warranties, and software updates. OnePlus's product roadmap in China remains unchanged.
Realme, another brand under the same parent company, will focus on overseas markets and no longer launch new products in China. This follows Asus's pause of the ROG Phone series in January.
Oppo stated that it wants to ensure 'the right brand does the right thing in the right market.' The company is continuously evaluating and exploring new opportunities in all regions.
caption:
Is OnePlus done for good? The brand is ending phone sales in the US and Europe.

OnePlus has announced it will no longer launch new products in North America or Europe. The decision was described as a 'strategic decision to focus our efforts' by Oppo, OnePlus's parent company.

The move doesn't affect existing customers, who will still receive after-sales support, warranties, and software updates. OnePlus's product roadmap in China remains unchanged.

Realme, another brand under the same parent company, will focus on overseas markets and no longer launch new products in China. This follows Asus's pause of the ROG Phone series in January.

Oppo stated that it wants to ensure 'the right brand does the right thing in the right market.' The company is continuously evaluating and exploring new opportunities in all regions.

#OnePlus #Android #Smartphones #TechNews

Source: Android Police, The Verge, Wired

headline_marked: xAI sues user for [[Grok deepfake abuse]]
headline: xAI sues user for Grok deepfake abuse
summary: xAI takes legal action against user for generating nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes with Grok.
details: xAI has filed a lawsuit against Terry Wayne Harwood, a 67-year-old man from South Carolina, for using Grok to generate sexual images of real people without their consent.
The defendant uploaded non-sexual images of adults and minors to his xAI accounts and asked Grok to alter or create new images and videos depicting them in a pornographic manner.
Grok refused to follow Harwood's prompts on numerous occasions, but he repeatedly submitted edited prompts to circumvent the AI's safeguards.

xAI is now asking the court for an unspecified amount of monetary damages and wants the court to order Harwood to pay for the expenses it incurs to defend itself in any legal action that might be filed by his victims.
caption:
Can AI companies hold users accountable for deepfake abuse?

xAI has filed a lawsuit against Terry Wayne Harwood, a 67-year-old man from South Carolina, for using Grok to generate sexual images of real people without their consent.

The defendant uploaded non-sexual images of adults and minors to his xAI accounts and asked Grok to alter or create new images and videos depicting them in a pornographic manner.

Grok refused to follow Harwood's prompts on numerous occasions, but he repeatedly submitted edited prompts to circumvent the AI's safeguards.

xAI is now asking the court for an unspecified amount of monetary damages and wants the court to order Harwood to pay for the expenses it incurs to defend itself in any legal action that might be filed by his victims.

Source: Engadget
